title: RBI Innovation Hub's MuleHunter.AI adopted by 23 banks; RBI declines to disclose mule accounts found
summary: By December 2025, 23 banks had adopted MuleHunter.AI to flag potential mule accounts. RBI withheld detection totals, so adoption does not establish fraud losses avoided.
account: MediaNama (Prabhanu Kumar Das) reported on 30 December 2025 on a Right to Information response. It showed 23 banks had implemented MuleHunter.AI as of 10 December 2025. That was up from at least 15 in August and nearly 20 in November 2025. The report named Canara Bank, Punjab National Bank, Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, AU Small Finance Bank and Federal Bank. The tool was developed by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH). It analyzes transaction and account patterns within each participating bank’s infrastructure to identify likely mule accounts. RBIH’s technical documentation says that personally identifiable information is not exchanged with the hub. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said that it cannot provide data on the number of mule accounts identified or acted upon through MuleHunter.AI. The reason given was that it holds such information in a fiduciary capacity with banks and disclosure could harm competitive interests. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra is reported as saying that the tool is showing a good success rate, without figures. An official May 12, 2026 release confirms an I4C-RBIH memorandum to use suspect identifiers and mule-account intelligence for model improvement. A later 31-bank deployment count remains unverified here.

fields.account: MediaNama (Prabhanu Kumar Das) reported on 30 December 2025 on a Right to Information response. It showed 23 banks had implemented MuleHunter.AI as of 10 December 2025. That was up from at least 15 in August and nearly 20 in November 2025. The report named Canara Bank, Punjab National Bank, Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, AU Small Finance Bank and Federal Bank. The tool was developed by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH). It analyzes transaction and account patterns within each participating bank’s infrastructure to identify likely mule accounts. RBIH’s technical documentation says that personally identifiable information is not exchanged with the hub. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) said that it cannot provide data on the number of mule accounts identified or acted upon through MuleHunter.AI. The reason given was that it holds such information in a fiduciary capacity with banks and disclosure could harm competitive interests. RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra is reported as saying that the tool is showing a good success rate, without figures. An official May 12, 2026 release confirms an I4C-RBIH memorandum to use suspect identifiers and mule-account intelligence for model improvement. A later 31-bank deployment count remains unverified here.
